meta.title: DIP-I-496: show role and permission for a logged-in user
meta.prompt: Propose a design for this ticket: DIP-I-496

answer: Show each permission group as a badge under the user's name in the account menu.

context.question: How does a logged-in user see which permission group they belong to, and where its guidelines are?
context.ask: A logged-in user cannot see which permission group they belong to, so they cannot find the guidelines that go with it.
product: In Administration, a permission group is a Group, shown in the Users table.
A user can belong to more than one group.
Users never see their group name, and some names are technical.
The Explorer account menu shows the avatar, name, email, Support and Logout.
context.gap: The account menu has no capture in app-context; its rows come from the attachment.

goals: A user reads their permission group in the account menu.
A group has a readable display name, not an internal key.
nonGoals: Changing who assigns groups; that stays in Administration.

findings.claim: Account menus show the role as a secondary identity signal under the name, never above it.
findings.source: SaaS Permissions and Roles UX Patterns, SaaSUI Design

findings.claim: The menu shows the compact signal; a profile page holds the full breakdown of scopes.
findings.source: Managing roles and permissions, flow examples, Nicelydone

findings.claim: Multi-role products summarise the count and let the user drill in instead of listing every permission.

screens.note: The account menu shows a My access row that expands to the groups and their catalog scope.

reasons.text: One group is the common case, and a badge answers it with no click.
Badges wrap cleanly when a user holds several groups; a text line does not.
The badge opens the panel that links to the guidelines.
Badges and expandable rows already exist in the kit, so nothing new is built.

pick.cost: To see catalogs or guidelines, a user still opens the My access panel.

openQuestions.text: Truncating a long group list needs a hover affordance the account menu does not carry today.
Who sets the display name on an existing permission group, and what it defaults to before anyone does.

change.adminSide: One optional Display name field on the create and edit group form, defaulting to the group name.
change.userSide: Group names show as badges under the name in the account menu.

latitude: Placement and visuals are open. Badges as the answer are not.
